title: Token flow mapping & alert playbook (QBR worksheet)
content:
Purpose:
This worksheet is designed to be an operational supplement for QBRs: visualize how tokens flow across a customer’s product surface, identify emergent billing risks, and propose precise alerting thresholds and remediation steps. The focus is on repeatable diagnostics (ingestion vs generation split, KV-cache hit impact, burst fingerprints) rather than raw top-line spend numbers.

How to use this sheet in a QBR (quick guide):
1) Pre-QBR ingestion (owner: CSM) - populate the Token Flow Map with last 90 days of logs, broken into 7-day rolling averages and 95th percentile spikes.
2) During QBR - walk the client through the Flow Map, highlight 2–3 anomalies (synthetic spikes, new endpoint rollout, model swap).
3) Action planning - set short-term alerts, medium-term rate-limit recommendations, owner & due dates.
4) Post-QBR - export the alert configuration to Ops and add a follow-up check 14 days after any threshold change.

Worksheet sections (tab names suggested):
- Overview (one-line executive summary + spend delta bullets)
- Token Flow Map (detailed breakdown by endpoint, direction, and model variant)
- Spike Scenarios (annotated intervals with suspected root cause)
- Alert Matrix (recommended thresholds + confidence + remediation steps)
- Rate Limit Impact Estimator (simulated user-visible errors and cost savings)
- Action Log (owners, tickets, due dates)

Token Flow Map (columns to import from logs):
- Date range: 2024-07-01 -> 2024-10-18 (example)
- Endpoint (route name)
- Direction: ingestion | generation | embedding
- Model variant: redwood-xx | open-yy | quantized-zz
- Calls: total requests
- Avg tokens in (per request)
- Avg tokens out (per request)
- KV-cache hit % (if applicable)
- Cost/token estimation ($)

Sample rows (text table):
Endpoint | Direction | Model | Calls | AvgIn | AvgOut | KVHit | EstimatedCost
chat-stream-v1 | generation | redwood-13b-q4 | 18,400 | 42 | 384 | 12% | $2,130
embed-bulk | embedding | open-embed-2 | 34,200 | 0 | 1536 | N/A | $1,224
summarize-api | ingestion | redwood-7b | 6,400 | 512 | 48 | 88% | $410

Interpretation heuristics (how to spot risk quickly):
- High AvgIn with low KV-hit: likely tokenizer/ingestion inefficiency (user sending large documents repeatedly).
- Large variance between median and 95th percentile: bursty behavior; check product release dates or scheduled jobs.
- Rapid model swaps to larger variants correlate to step-change in spend; recommend model gating for canary users.

Spike Scenarios (what to annotate in QBR):
- Scheduled release: annotate deploy time + new route attribution.
- Third-party ingestion misconfiguration: repeated large in requests from a single API key.
- Looping customer processes: repeated failed runs causing retries (look at http status + latency).

Alert Matrix (recommended columns):
- Alert name
- Trigger metric (e.g., 95p tokens/day per API key; avg tokens/request across route; calls per minute)
- Threshold value (numeric)
- Sensitivity (low | medium | high)
- Expected false positives per week (estimate)
- Recommended action (automated: throttle | notify CSM | disable key)
- Owner (CSM / Dev / Ops)
- Escalation path / SLA
- Notes (why this threshold)

Example alert entries (text):
Name: high-95p-token-APIKEY
Trigger: 95th percentile tokens/day per API key > 50k
Threshold: 50,000
Sensitivity: medium
Expected FP/wk: 0–1
Action: create automated email to CSM + create Ops ticket to investigate; apply soft rate-limit for 1 hour if persists
Owner: CSM (Priya)
Escalation: Ops on-call -> Engineering (SRE)
Notes: threshold chosen based on client’s production baseline + 25% buffer

Rate Limit Impact Estimator (instructions):
- Inputs: baseline calls/min, 95p tokens/request, top 3 offending API keys
- Outputs: estimated user errors per minute when applying X% throttle, monthly cost savings estimate, customer-visible impact score (1 low — 5 high)
- Use the estimator during the QBR to show tradeoffs between immediate cost control vs potential product friction.

Remediation playbook snippets (templated actions):
- If ingestion inefficiency: suggest adding client-side dedup, batching or compression; propose a canary of dedup in staging for 2 weeks.
- If embeddings bulk spikes: propose a cache layer or pre-commit batching; recommend migration to cheaper embedding variant for non-critical workloads.
- If model upgrade caused step-change: propose pinning to prior variant for non-canary users and a staged rollout.

Suggested conversation script for the QBR (CSM talking points):
1) "Here’s how tokens are flowing across your product — we see 3 main contributors: chat, embeddings, and nightly analytics jobs."
2) "Two notable spikes are annotated: Aug 2 (release A) and Sep 12 (ingestion misconfig) — both explain ~38% of the month-over-month increase."
3) "We recommend three actions: a short-term alert, a medium-term rate-limit on the offending API key, and a longer play to reduce AvgIn via batching. Who on your side can own the batching work?"

Action log template (columns):
- Action ID
- Short description
- Owner (CS or Customer Eng)
- Priority (P0|P1|P2)
- Due date
- Status (open|in_progress|done)
- Linked ticket (Jira/GH)

Recommended follow-ups after QBR:
- 7 days: confirm alert configuration deployed and sending notifications
- 14 days: measure 7d rolling cost delta and customer-visible error rate
- 30 days: consider permanent rate limit or model rollback if cost remains elevated

Notes & known limitations:
- Cost estimation here is rough; for contract-level billing reconciliations always defer to Finance exports (billing CSV).
- KV-cache percentage relies on token-level tracing enabled in the runtime; if not available, substitute with inferred cache-effect using median latency and token-in column.
- This sheet assumes access to per-key and per-route logs; if you only have aggregate billing, run a quick log ingest job to build the Flow Map before the QBR.

Appendix: quick import checklist for CSM
- Raw log pulls: start_date, end_date, fields (timestamp, api_key, route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, status, latency)
- Derive 95th percentile tokens/day per api_key and 95p tokens/request per route
- Populate sample rows and confirm KV cache column (or mark N/A)
- Draft two suggested alerts with owners and put in Action Log

Template export options: CSV for the Token Flow Map, PDF summary for executive slide deck, JSON for sending alert configurations to Ops via webhooks.

Open questions to resolve (for team):
- Do we want a standard conservative threshold set per product vertical? (finance vs consumer apps differ)
- Should we include a friction score that quantifies UX impact of throttles (requires product input)?
- Can we automate the recommended remedial actions into the console as a one-click mitigation?

---
Editors: Elena Ruiz (owner) — keep this as the canonical draft for the next 2 QBR cycles.
